newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG ANXIOUSLY EYE METZ CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG ANXIOUSLY EYE METZ CLASH.

text.p: Victory at the weekend saw Paris St Germain go top of the French first division, but the side from the capital are anxiously eyeing this Friday's visit to second-placed Metz.

On Saturday the Parisians beat a visiting Cannes team 3-1 to maintain their 100 percent record of three wins from three matches, but looked shaky in the process, and must improve to beat the only other unbeaten side in the French top flight.
"We were lacking stamina. We were late for every ball in the first half," PSG coach Ricardo said.
And he moaned that his players appeared tired after their Champion's League qualifying defeat at Steaua Bucharest on Wednesday.
The Parisians have the best attacking line-up on paper, having scored at least two goals in their last four outings, but must deal with defensive frailties before travelling to ambitious Metz.
Paris have conceded a goal in each of their three league matches and a trio in their 3-2 defeat in Bucharest.
"We have a week to work this problem out", Ricardo said. "I saw Metz playing on television on Friday and I must say they have a much better team than last season."
Metz, who clinched their second away-win when they beat promoted Chateauroux 2-1 last Friday, are second to PSG on goal difference.
"I'm not surprised by their position in the table and I think they can be considered as probable rivals in the title race", Ricardo said.
Metz have been beaten at home by PSG for the past two seasons and are anxious to break their Parisian jinx.

"We have to be very careful in our strategic choices to avoid the mistakes we made the past two years. Playing the PSG is always a special match for us", midfielder Jocelyn Blanchard said. "A defeat is not allowed."
Metz coach Joel Muller sees this Friday's match and the following clash, against Monaco, as real tests for his side.
"I think that we are better armed and better prepared than the previous seasons and I don't think we are going to lose", he predicted.
Title holders Monaco, who had a solitary point after their first two matches, recovered their stylish brand of play when they easily won 3-0 at Lyon on Saturday.
The French champions moved from 17th to joint seventh in the league and are now five points behind their Parisian arch-rivals. Monaco visit third from bottom Rennes on Friday.
